Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is her jacket fully closed?
node.criteria: The jacket’s front panels are brought together so no visible opening remains along its closure.
node.binding: Compare the jacket on the woman in SOURCE with the jacket on the woman in EDITED; the requested endpoint is a fully closed jacket.
node.endpoint: Her jacket is fully closed, with no visible opening along the closure.
node.necessity: This is the requested change and its complete endpoint.
node.zero_when: The jacket shows no requested progress toward closure compared with SOURCE.
node.half_when: The jacket is partly closed, with concrete progress toward closure but a visible opening remaining.
node.full_when: The jacket is fully closed, with no visible opening remaining along its closure.

node_traces.evidence: In SOURCE, the jacket is open at the front. In EDITED, it remains visibly open, with the front panels separated and one panel hanging outward; there is no visible progress toward bringing the panels together.

response.content: {"text":"The node’s binding already targets the requested endpoint, but its zero criterion is too coarse: “no requested progress” can collapse a partially obscured or ambiguous closure into a confident no. In these images the edited subject is turned sideways and the jacket front is largely hidden by the draped panel, so the trace’s claim that the panels remain separated and show no progress is not clearly verifiable; the 0.94 confidence is not supported by visible closure evidence. Refine the comparison to inspect the closure itself in both images and distinguish visible progress from complete closure, while treating an occluded or indeterminate closure as unresolved rather than inferring absence of progress. Preserve the rubric’s partial category and do not count the pose or unrelated changes as jacket progress. The trace is valid, queried, and dependency-free, so this is a visual-evidence/criterion issue, not a transport or schema failure."}
